newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via customer or system RP.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via customer or system RP.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the U.S. banking system on Wednesday via either customer or overnight system repurchase agreements, Fed watchers said.

"Today is the last day of the (two-week reserve maintenance) period and the Fed has three sets of system RPs outstanding: the 14-day, the three-day and the two-day," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"So our numbers suggest the Fed can get by with a customer RP ... But I do need to note the risk of an overnight system since funds are trading well above target," Saporta added.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International Inc expect the central bank to add reserves through an overnight system repurchase agreement operation.
At 1030 EDT/1430 GMT, federal funds changed hands at 5-1/2 percent, well above the central bank's 5-1/4 percent target.
